frames.action: press 'Up' -- move the selection off the ready-made characters and onto the one I fill in myself
frames.commentary: None of these ready-made people are me. Up one, where I answer for myself.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- take the entry that lets me fill myself in by hand
frames.commentary: Right. Let us see what I look like written down.

frames.action: press 'f' -- finish the world settings as the engine offered them
frames.commentary: Fairport Harbor. I have run gear out of a dozen towns with that kind of name.

frames.action: press 'Y' -- answer the case-sensitive confirmation with the capital it wants
frames.commentary: Yes. The shape of the world is not mine to argue with.

frames.action: press 'shift+Tab' -- step back to the points page before I choose anything about myself
frames.commentary: Before I answer anything, let me see what the answers cost.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- move down off the no-limits budget onto the one with separate pools
frames.commentary: A version of me with no limits is not a person, it is a wish. Down one.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- take the budget where every gain has to be paid for somewhere else
frames.commentary: Strong in one place is paid for in another. I would rather see the bill.

frames.action: press 'Tab' -- move on to where this starts
frames.commentary: Right. Now where does this begin.

frames.action: press 'slash' -- open the search on the list of starts
frames.commentary: There is a long list here and I already know which one is mine.

frames.action: press 'm' -- begin spelling the start I am looking for
frames.commentary: M. I know the word for what happened to me.

frames.action: press 'i' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: I. It is a short word and it is the true one.

frames.action: press 's' -- finish spelling it
frames.commentary: S. Missed. That is the honest word for what happened to me.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see what is left of the list
frames.commentary: Show me what is left when I ask for that.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- take the start that matches what actually happened to me
frames.commentary: I was on the water when it started. I came back to a harbour with nobody left.

frames.action: press 'Tab' -- move on to what I actually am
frames.commentary: That is settled then. Now the trade.

frames.action: press 'slash' -- open the search on the trades
frames.commentary: I know the answer to this one without reading the list.

frames.action: press 'f' -- begin spelling my trade
frames.commentary: F. The same word my father put on his own papers.

frames.action: press 'i' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: I. Four letters, and they cover my whole life.

frames.action: press 's' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: S. Nearly there, and I have never wanted another.

frames.action: press 'h' -- finish spelling it
frames.commentary: H. Fisher. Thirty-one seasons of it.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see what is left
frames.commentary: Show me.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- take the trade I actually have
frames.commentary: A rod, a knife, waders, and my father's watch. That last I would fight for.

frames.action: press 'Tab' -- move on from the trade
frames.commentary: That is me on paper. What else do they want.

frames.action: press 'slash' -- open the search on the other things I am
frames.commentary: Two habits I will not pretend about, and both of them are on this page.

frames.action: press 'n' -- begin spelling the first of them
frames.commentary: N. Start with the one I am least proud of.

frames.action: press 'i' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: I. No sense hiding it; it is on my breath.

frames.action: press 'c' -- finish spelling it
frames.commentary: C. Nicotine. Since I was nineteen.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see what is left
frames.commentary: Show me.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- take the habit I have had since I was nineteen
frames.commentary: Smoking since nineteen. It will cost me a bad head, and then worse.

frames.action: press 'slash' -- open the search again for the other habit
frames.commentary: And the other one.

frames.action: press 'c' -- begin spelling it
frames.commentary: C. And the other thing I have always run on.

frames.action: press 'a' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: A. Every galley I worked in had a pot going.

frames.action: press 'f' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: F. Spell it out and let it stand against me.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see the two that match
frames.commentary: Show me both of them.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- move off the extreme version of it onto the plain one
frames.commentary: No. I drink it black and plenty of it, but it never made me strange.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- take the plain coffee habit
frames.commentary: Black and too much of it for thirty years. Two days of headache, then fine.

frames.action: press 'slash' -- open the search once more, to take something off the list
frames.commentary: There is one on there that is not true of me.

frames.action: press 'BackSpace' -- rub out the old search; nothing on the screen changed
frames.commentary: Clear that out first.

frames.action: press 'h' -- type over the selected search text instead of trying to rub it out
frames.commentary: H. Over the top of it, then.

frames.action: press 'i' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: I. The schooling I never finished.

frames.action: press 'g' -- finish spelling it
frames.commentary: G. High school.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see what it found
frames.commentary: Show me.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- take the schooling back off the list, because I never had it
frames.commentary: I left school at sixteen for the boats. I will not write myself a diploma.

frames.action: press 'slash' -- open the search for the one piece of paper I do have
frames.commentary: There is one licence on that list I have actually held in my hand.

frames.action: press 'b' -- type over what the box is holding
frames.commentary: B. Now the one piece of paper I did earn.

frames.action: press 'o' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: O. Nine years of it, and I earned every one.

frames.action: press 'a' -- finish spelling it
frames.commentary: A. Boating.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- close the search
frames.commentary: Show me.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- take the boating licence, because I have held one for nine years
frames.commentary: Nine years with my own boat. Forty-two feet, and a diesel I rebuilt twice.

frames.action: press 'Tab' -- move on to the honest part
frames.commentary: Now the part where I put a number on myself.

frames.action: press 'plus' -- put strength up where it belongs
frames.commentary: Thirty-one years hauling traps over a gunwale. Nobody would argue with it.

frames.action: press 'plus' -- and once more
frames.commentary: I can still put a full trap on the rail. Ten, and that is all I claim.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- move down past the hands
frames.commentary: My hands are ordinary. Never quick, only steady, and steady is not listed.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- and down again, to the schooling I never had
frames.commentary: Here is where I pay for the boats.

frames.action: press 'minus' -- take a point off the book-learning, which I never had
frames.commentary: School ended at sixteen. Anything out of a book comes to me slowly.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- move down to what I got instead
frames.commentary: And here is what I got instead of schooling.

frames.action: press 'plus' -- put my eyes up where they actually are
frames.commentary: I can read a change in the water at half a mile. That I will claim.

frames.action: press 'plus' -- and once more, and that is the last of it
frames.commentary: I notice things before I have decided to. Ten, and I will not gild it past that.

frames.action: press 'Tab' -- move on to what is wrong with me, and what is right
frames.commentary: Now the part I put off. I would rather know my weight than flatter it.

frames.action: press 'slash' -- open the search on the list of what I am
frames.commentary: Start with the thing that will put me on the floor.

frames.action: press 'b' -- begin spelling the first honest thing
frames.commentary: B. Four letters for six years of trouble.

frames.action: press 'a' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: A. The first thing a doctor ever wrote about me.

frames.action: press 'c' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: C. No use pretending it will hold out here.

frames.action: press 'k' -- finish spelling it
frames.commentary: K. My back.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see it written down
frames.commentary: There it is, in a list, like a diagnosis.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- take the back, because it is the truest thing about me
frames.commentary: Six years of it. There is a way of lifting that puts me on the deck.

frames.action: press 'slash' -- open the search again
frames.commentary: And the other thing I have always known about myself.

frames.action: press 's' -- type over the old search
frames.commentary: S. The other thing thirty-one seasons gave me.

frames.action: press 'l' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: L. A mercy on the boat and a danger on land.

frames.action: press 'e' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: E. Better on the page than a surprise later.

frames.action: press 'e' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: E again.

frames.action: press 'p' -- finish spelling it
frames.commentary: P. How I sleep.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see what it found
frames.commentary: Show me.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- take the sleeping, which was a mercy on the boat and will not be one now
frames.commentary: Thirty-one years in a bunk over a diesel. No noise has ever woken me.

frames.action: press 'slash' -- open the search once more
frames.commentary: One more honest thing, and then the other column.

frames.action: press 'a' -- type over the old search
frames.commentary: A. The word my mother's family never said aloud.

frames.action: press 'd' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: D. Say it plainly, the way she never could.

frames.action: press 'd' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: D again.

frames.action: press 'i' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: I. Halfway through a word I have watched do damage.

frames.action: press 'c' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: C. Two letters left and no excuse ready.

frames.action: press 't' -- finish spelling it
frames.commentary: T. It runs straight down my mother's side of the family.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see what it found
frames.commentary: Show me.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- move off the resistant one, which I am plainly not
frames.commentary: That is the wrong way round. I am not the resistant kind and never have been.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- take the streak that runs in my family
frames.commentary: Coffee and cigarettes ran the boats. It cost me something I loved already.

frames.action: press 'slash' -- open the search for the other column
frames.commentary: Now what is right with me. There are fewer, and I will not pad the list.

frames.action: press 't' -- type over the old search
frames.commentary: T. Something in my favour, for once.

frames.action: press 'o' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: O. It is not modesty; there are only three.

frames.action: press 'u' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: U. Thirty-one seasons put this one into me.

frames.action: press 'g' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: G. One letter short of the only boast I make.

frames.action: press 'h' -- finish spelling it
frames.commentary: H. I do not break easily.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see what it found
frames.commentary: Show me.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- take the toughness, which is thirty-one seasons and not a gift
frames.commentary: Thrown against a gunwale in February and back at work by the afternoon.

frames.action: press 'slash' -- open the search again
frames.commentary: Ask it again. There is one more that is true.

frames.action: press 's' -- type over the old search
frames.commentary: S. The one nobody believes until they sail with me.

frames.action: press 't' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: T. Bait boxes, three-day chowder, and never once ill.

frames.action: press 'o' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: O. Not a boast, only thirty-one years of proof.

frames.action: press 'm' -- finish spelling it
frames.commentary: M. My stomach.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see what it found
frames.commentary: Show me.

frames.action: press 'Up' -- move up off the weak one
frames.commentary: No. The opposite of that, in fact.

frames.action: press 'Up' -- and up again, to the one that is true
frames.commentary: There. That one.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- take the stomach that has never once betrayed me
frames.commentary: Bait-box sandwiches and three-day chowder. None of it ever came back up.

frames.action: press 'slash' -- open the search for the last of them
frames.commentary: One more, and it is the one people always get wrong about me.

frames.action: press 'p' -- type over the old search
frames.commentary: P. Everything I own has one place it goes.

frames.action: press 'a' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: A. That is what a small boat teaches you.

frames.action: press 'c' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: C. My back will still charge me for it.

frames.action: press 'k' -- finish spelling it
frames.commentary: K. What I can carry.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see what it found
frames.commentary: Show me.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- take the packing, which is a lifetime of stowing gear in a small boat
frames.commentary: Everything aboard has one place it goes. My back pays; I know how to stow.

frames.action: press 'Tab' -- move on to what I can actually do
frames.commentary: That is the whole of what I am. Now what I can do with it.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- start down the list of things a person can be good at
frames.commentary: Bashing things with a stick is not a trade. Past it.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- down again, onto getting out of the way
frames.commentary: Knives are for fish and rope. Here is the one that has actually kept me alive.

frames.action: press 'plus' -- buy the getting out of the way
frames.commentary: What kills people out there is being in a rush. I let things go past me.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- keep going down, past the fighting
frames.commentary: Dodging reads two now. Past the hand-to-hand.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- past the spears as well
frames.commentary: Nor that.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- and past fighting with my hands
frames.commentary: I have never hit anybody in my life and I am not going to start claiming I know how.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- past the bows
frames.commentary: The bar is on unarmed now. No.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- past the handguns
frames.commentary: Archery. My father would have laughed.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- past the pistols
frames.commentary: There was a flare pistol in the locker. That is all I know of firearms.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- past whatever a launcher is
frames.commentary: Launchers. I would not know which end to hold.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- past the marksmanship
frames.commentary: Marksmanship. No.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- past the rifles
frames.commentary: Rifles. No.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- past the shotguns
frames.commentary: A man two slips down kept one aboard. I thought it foolish to have.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- past the machine guns
frames.commentary: Whatever a submachine gun is, it is not mine.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- past the throwing
frames.commentary: I can throw a line. That is not the same thing and I will not pretend it is.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- past the science
frames.commentary: Applied science. That is for people who stayed in school.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- past the wiring
frames.commentary: I can rewire a bilge pump and that is the end of my electrics.

frames.action: press 'plus' -- buy the mending
frames.commentary: Nets, line, canvas, a half-rotten hull made sound. This one I have earned.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- move on to the cooking
frames.commentary: Fabrication reads two of mine on top of the one I already had. Next.

frames.action: press 'plus' -- buy the cooking
frames.commentary: Whatever came up in the net, in a pan. Nine years of feeding a crew.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- move on down the page
frames.commentary: Food handling is bought. On.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- past the survival, which the trade already gave me
frames.commentary: Five came with the trade already. I will not buy more of what I have.

frames.action: press 'plus' -- buy the needlework
frames.commentary: Every stitch in my own oilskins is mine. Aboard, that job was always mine.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- on to the swimming
frames.commentary: Tailoring is bought. Next.

frames.action: press 'plus' -- buy the swimming and the wind
frames.commentary: Twice over the side in nine years and twice back aboard. No wind to run.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- on down past the computers
frames.commentary: Athletics reads two and two. Two things left that I have actually done.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- and past whatever devices are
frames.commentary: A telephone is a telephone. I do not need a level in it.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- on to the patching-up
frames.commentary: Devices, whatever that means. Past it.

frames.action: press 'plus' -- buy the patching-up
frames.commentary: Hooks through a hand, rope burn, a man short two fingers. I patched them.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- on to the last one
frames.commentary: Health care is bought. One thing left, and it is the one I am proudest of.

frames.action: press 'plus' -- buy the diesel work
frames.commentary: I rebuilt that diesel twice. A bad bearing I can usually hear and fix.

frames.action: press 'at' -- put right what it has me down as
frames.commentary: It has me down as a man. I am a woman, and fifty-two years of one.

frames.action: press 'dollar' -- and dress me accordingly
frames.commentary: And put me in my own clothes while it is at it.

frames.action: press 'a' -- ask it how old I am
frames.commentary: Fifty-two years, and most of them wet.

frames.action: press '5' -- type over the number it guessed
frames.commentary: Five. Whatever it guessed, this is the true number.

frames.action: press '2' -- finish the number
frames.commentary: Two. Fifty-two.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- set my age down
frames.commentary: Fifty-two. Thirty-one seasons out of Gloucester, nine on my own boat.

frames.action: press 'n' -- ask it what to call me
frames.commentary: They ought to know what to call me.

frames.action: press 'O' -- begin my given name
frames.commentary: O. The name my mother chose, and I will spell it whole.

frames.action: press 'd' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: D. Slowly, the way she used to say it.

frames.action: press 'e' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: E. Three letters in and it already sounds like her.

frames.action: press 't' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: T. Halfway. It is a long name for a deck hand.

frames.action: press 't' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: T again.

frames.action: press 'e' -- finish my given name
frames.commentary: E. Odette. Everyone who ever mattered called me Dette.

frames.action: press 'space' -- leave a gap before my father's name; nothing on the screen changed
frames.commentary: And his name after mine.

frames.action: press 'V' -- begin the family name
frames.commentary: V. The name that came down from my grandfather.

frames.action: press 'a' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: A. Six letters, and two countries inside them.

frames.action: press 'c' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: C. I have never shortened it for anybody's convenience.

frames.action: press 'h' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: H. My father wore this name on his licence too.

frames.action: press 'o' -- keep spelling it
frames.commentary: O. One letter left, and then I am somebody again.

frames.action: press 'n' -- finish the family name
frames.commentary: N. Vachon. My grandfather brought it down from Riviere-du-Loup in a duffel bag.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- set my name down
frames.commentary: Odette Vachon. Out of Gloucester, and before that Riviere-du-Loup.

frames.action: press 'Tab' -- look over the whole of it before I say yes to it
frames.commentary: Let me see all of it laid out before I sign my name to it.

frames.action: press 'Tab' -- say that this is the whole of me
frames.commentary: Strong, slow, sharp-eyed, and not one weapon on the page. That is me.

frames.action: press 'Y' -- answer the case-sensitive question with the capital it wants
frames.commentary: Yes. Camille teaches in Salem and I will not learn that from in here.

frames.action: press 'V' -- find out what is in here with me before I move a foot
frames.commentary: First thing in a strange room: find out if anything is looking back.

frames.action: press 'Escape' -- close the list, having got my answer
frames.commentary: Nothing alive in here but me. I will take that and stop counting caps.

frames.action: press 'm' -- look at the chart and find out where in the world I have washed up
frames.commentary: Thirty-one years of reading charts first. I want to know where water is.

frames.action: press 'Escape' -- close the chart
frames.commentary: West Rutland, and not a drop of salt water anywhere. I am well inland.

frames.action: press 'bar' -- stand still and listen before I touch anything
frames.commentary: Sit tight and listen. That is most of what fishing ever was.

frames.action: press 'w' -- choose to wait rather than set the alarm
frames.commentary: My father's watch has an alarm. Waiting is what I want from it now.

frames.action: press '3' -- wait five minutes and listen to the building
frames.commentary: Five minutes. If anything in here heard me, it will say so by then.

frames.action: press 'Y' -- stop the wait, because that sound is worth answering
frames.commentary: Gargling. That is a throat that no longer works, and it is close.

frames.action: press 'V' -- take a sounding: find out whether the thing to the northwest can be seen from here
frames.commentary: Northwest, and northwest of me is a shut door. Take a sounding first.

frames.action: press 'Tab' -- turn the list from goods to living things
frames.commentary: Caps, balls, a till nobody wants. None of that is what I asked for.

frames.action: press 'Tab' -- turn the list again, to what the building is made of
frames.commentary: Nothing alive on the page, and I heard it plain. It is behind a wall.

frames.action: press 'Escape' -- close the survey, having learned the thing I did not want to learn
frames.commentary: Twenty-six racks, eight windows, and not one tap in the whole building.

frames.action: press 'Right' -- walk east off the open carpet, toward the goods and away from the shut door I heard through
frames.commentary: Get off this carpet. East, toward the light, with furniture between us.

frames.action: press 'Right' -- keep going east, off the carpet and onto the shop floor
frames.commentary: One step and I have already made noise. Nothing to do but keep going.

frames.action: press 'Right' -- one more step east, to stand alongside the racks
frames.commentary: Cloth hanging on the rack below. I stop beside them, not into them.

frames.action: press 'g' -- reach for what is on the rack beside me instead of walking into it
frames.commentary: Cloth on a rack, and nothing on my arms. Skin covered is skin kept.

frames.action: press 'greater' -- open the bag up before deciding whether to carry it; nothing on the screen changed
frames.commentary: A bag is also whatever stands in it. Look inside before I heave it up.

frames.action: press 'W' -- put the empty bag on rather than carry it in my hands
frames.commentary: Empty. But it is space, and space I have none of. Over the shoulder.

frames.action: press 'Up' -- work north up the aisle toward the counter and the desks
frames.commentary: Four pounds heavier already. Now the counter, where the useful things go.

frames.action: press 'Up' -- keep north along the open floor beside the racks
frames.commentary: Quiet as waders allow. This floor tells the room exactly where I am.

frames.action: press 'Up' -- north again, two paces off the counter now
frames.commentary: Two seconds for that step, not one. Something underfoot, or the bag.

frames.action: press 'Up' -- one more north, up level with the counter
frames.commentary: The till stands open with fifteen dollars in it. I want a bottle instead.

frames.action: press 'g' -- reach across the counter for whatever is lying on it; nothing in the map column changed
frames.commentary: A car. A whole car out on the tarmac. But the counter first, in order.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- turn round and head south down the aisle for the door in the east wall
frames.commentary: Nothing but dollars I cannot drink. The car, and by a door not a window.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- south again
frames.commentary: One pace, one second. On the water you count seconds too, for weather.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- south past the last of the racks
frames.commentary: The green thing is still on the rack. I mark it and come back if I can.

frames.action: press 'n' -- try to cut southeast and be refused by a rack I had miscounted
frames.commentary: I go to cut the corner and the rack stops me. I counted the line wrong.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- straight south instead, since the rack will not let me cut
frames.commentary: Straight down the aisle then, and no more cleverness. The rack wins that argument.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- south again, past the green garment on the rack
frames.commentary: A jacket on the end of the line. Two paces off my way if I come back.

frames.action: press 'n' -- try the diagonal again now the racks really have ended
frames.commentary: Now the line has ended for certain. I will take the corner I was refused.

frames.action: press 'n' -- step southeast toward the pale shape standing against the east wall
frames.commentary: Pale and squat by the wall. A bin, or a basin with an inch left in it.

frames.action: press 'e' -- put a hand on the pale shape rather than guess at it from across the room; nothing in the map column changed
frames.commentary: Close enough now to reach it. I will not guess. Guessing is how people drown.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- leave the pale shape alone and drop south toward the door
frames.commentary: Nothing in it. There is no water in a golf shop and I knew that.

frames.action: press 'n' -- southeast into the dark corner in front of the door
frames.commentary: A patch of dark in front of the door. Better it does not see me first.

frames.action: press 'o' -- open the door properly instead of shouldering it
frames.commentary: Hand on the handle, not a shoulder. Quiet out means quiet back in.

frames.action: press 'Right' -- step into the open doorway and look out before going any further
frames.commentary: It swung without a sound. Stand in the gap and look before crossing.

frames.action: press 'Right' -- step out of the doorway onto the sidewalk
frames.commentary: Three red cars and nobody on the tarmac. Steady, no running, eyes up.

frames.action: press 'n' -- angle southeast across the tarmac toward the near car
frames.commentary: Out in the open with nothing between me and the treeline. Quickly.

frames.action: press 'n' -- second diagonal southeast
frames.commentary: Tarmac under waders is a sound I will not learn to like.

frames.action: press 'n' -- third diagonal, lining up on the car's flank
frames.commentary: Third one. My back is already telling me about a bag with nothing in it.

frames.action: press 'Right' -- straight east now, at the car's flank
frames.commentary: Four seats, a whole screen, the boot toward me. People forget boots.

frames.action: press 'Right' -- east again
frames.commentary: Two seconds a pace out here. Waders were never made for tarmac.

frames.action: press 'Right' -- east once more, over the painted line
frames.commentary: Over the yellow line. Nobody is left to mind the gap it was painted for.

frames.action: press 'g' -- reach into the car for whatever is stowed in it; nothing in the map column changed
frames.commentary: Close enough to touch the paint. Let us see what a golfer leaves behind.

frames.action: press 'Right' -- one more east, right up against the paintwork
frames.commentary: A painted bay line between me and it. My arm is not that long. One more.

frames.action: press 'e' -- put a hand on the car and see what it will tell me
frames.commentary: Warm already where the sun has been on it. Now find out what is inside.

frames.action: press 'Right' -- answer the direction prompt with east, where the car is
frames.commentary: A squirrel, east, and my mouth watered. It will not hold still for me.

frames.action: press 'e' -- choose to examine the vehicle rather than just mark where it is
frames.commentary: It offers to remember where the car is. I know where the car is.

frames.action: press 'Escape' -- close the car down, having learned what it is and what it is not
frames.commentary: Faulty motor, bare boot, petrol I cannot carry. Four dry seats, though.

frames.action: press 'V' -- survey the ground from out here in the open, where I can see
frames.commentary: A golf course has a pond in it. I have a rod and fifteen baits.

frames.action: press 'Tab' -- turn the survey past the goods
frames.commentary: Goods first, always. I do not want goods. I want a shape of water.

frames.action: press 'Tab' -- and past the living things, to the ground itself
frames.commentary: Not goods. Not the living. The ground. Show me the ground.

frames.action: press 'Tab' -- come back round to the ground and read the rest of it
frames.commentary: Eight hundred tiles of forest and a hundred and eighty of underbrush.

frames.action: press 'Next' -- page down the ground list to the part I could not see
frames.commentary: Turn the page. If there is water here it will be in the far half.

frames.action: press 'Next' -- page down again, further into the far half
frames.commentary: Forest floor six paces south. A wood in May has things a woman can eat.

frames.action: press 'Next' -- and again, to the bottom of the list
frames.commentary: Keep going. The greens are at the far end, and water follows greens.

frames.action: press 'Next' -- one more page, to the very bottom
frames.commentary: Sixty-eight of green, three flags, a whole wood, and still no water.

frames.action: press 'Next' -- the last page of the ground
frames.commentary: Nine willows. Willow keeps its feet wet. That means standing water.

frames.action: press 'Escape' -- close the survey and go to the wood, since the wood is what I can reach
frames.commentary: No water in fifty-nine kinds of ground. But underbrush is seven paces.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- south off the tarmac toward the wood
frames.commentary: South. Off the tarmac, over the kerb, into the green.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- south off the tarmac toward the wood
frames.commentary: South again. The green is where the food is, if any is.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- south off the tarmac toward the wood
frames.commentary: And again. My back would rather walk than stand still.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- over the kerb onto the grass
frames.commentary: The kerb, and then real ground. A leafy thing four paces down.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- down onto the grass proper
frames.commentary: Grass. My knees are grateful and my back is not, and both are right.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- two more paces to the leafy plant
frames.commentary: Softer underfoot and quieter, which suits me. Two more paces.

frames.action: press 'Down' -- up alongside the plant
frames.commentary: Grass takes two seconds a pace where tarmac took one. Thicker than it looks.

frames.action: press 'e' -- get my hands into the underbrush and search it
frames.commentary: I am standing in it. Patience is most of the difference between meals.

frames.action: press 'Y' -- answer yes and forage the underbrush
frames.commentary: Yes. Yes, of course yes.

frames.action: press 'g' -- gather up what the underbrush gave me
frames.commentary: Two handfuls of leaves. Greens hold water, and water I have none of.

frames.action: press 'a' -- mark the leaves so I can take them
frames.commentary: There they are, listed as mine to take. Mark them.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- confirm and take the leaves
frames.commentary: Marked. Take them.

frames.action: press 'n' -- southeast, toward the next patch of broad leaves
frames.commentary: Two handfuls is not a day's eating. Another patch six along and two down.

frames.action: press 'n' -- southeast again, down to the road's edge
frames.commentary: Three seconds to get out. Getting out costs what getting in did.

frames.action: press 'Right' -- east along the edge of the grass
frames.commentary: East along the seam where grass meets tarmac. I can see both ways.

frames.action: press 'Right' -- east again
frames.commentary: The road below runs east and west and nothing is moving on it.

frames.action: press 'Right' -- east, third pace
frames.commentary: Three. Nearly on it.

frames.action: press 'e' -- search the second patch without stepping into it
frames.commentary: Beside it now. I will search it from here rather than wade in again.

frames.action: press 'm' -- put the chart up now that I have walked a little of it
frames.commentary: Nothing in that one. Two nets come up full and the third holds a boot.

frames.action: press 'Up' -- walk the chart north a square at a time and read what each one is called
frames.commentary: The course lies north, four squares deep, with pale blue at the top.

frames.action: press 'Up' -- north again on the chart
frames.commentary: The square above me is the car park itself. Of course it is. Keep going north.

frames.action: press 'Up' -- north onto the course itself
frames.commentary: Car park, then the course. Two squares up and I am on the fairway.

frames.action: press 'Up' -- north again, still on the course
frames.commentary: Still the course. It is a big one.

frames.action: press 'Up' -- one more north, to the pale blue square
frames.commentary: Four squares of golf course. One more and I am on the blue.

frames.action: press 'Left' -- one square west, onto the blue
frames.commentary: A forest trail is a way through a wood without fighting the wood.

frames.action: press 'N' -- put a mark on the chart where the water is
frames.commentary: Swamp. Five squares north, and nine willows saying it from the ground.

frames.action: press 'W' -- begin writing the mark
frames.commentary: I do not need a colour. I need five letters I will trust at first light.

frames.action: press 'A' -- second letter
frames.commentary: W. A woman writing on a chart with one finger, like my father did.

frames.action: press 'T' -- third letter
frames.commentary: W, A. He wrote his in pencil so he could rub out a mark when a bank shifted.

frames.action: press 'E' -- fourth letter
frames.commentary: W, A, T.

frames.action: press 'R' -- last letter
frames.commentary: W, A, T, E. One more and it is written down where it cannot fall out of my head.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- set the mark down on the chart
frames.commentary: WATER, on the chart and out of my head, where I cannot lose it.

frames.action: press 'Escape' -- put the chart away and start back for the door
frames.commentary: Tomorrow is settled. Nothing to carry water in, so home and shut the door.

frames.action: press 'y' -- northwest, back the way I came
frames.commentary: Thirteen east and twelve south to walk back. Round the cars, not through.

frames.action: press 'y' -- northwest again
frames.commentary: Two seconds a pace on grass. It adds up, and my back is keeping the tally.

frames.action: press 'y' -- northwest, third stride
frames.commentary: Out, round a car, down to the road and back. A morning's work already.

frames.action: press 'y' -- northwest onto the kerb
frames.commentary: Over the kerb onto the hard stuff. Quick walking and loud walking both.

frames.action: press 'y' -- northwest onto the tarmac, passing west of the car
frames.commentary: Both its doors hang open like a gutted fish. I go up the west side.

frames.action: press 'y' -- northwest again across the lot
frames.commentary: A second a pace on tarmac against two on grass. One small favour.

frames.action: press 'y' -- northwest, third of eight
frames.commentary: Two seconds that one, so I have crossed a painted line. Three down, five to go.

frames.action: press 'y' -- northwest, fourth
frames.commentary: Halfway. The wall is on my left with its windows gone dark.

frames.action: press 'y' -- northwest, fifth
frames.commentary: Five. The door is three more on the slant, if I have counted right.

frames.action: press 'y' -- northwest, sixth
frames.commentary: There it is, black and open, with the bin inside and the racks beyond.

frames.action: press 'y' -- northwest, seventh
frames.commentary: Two more.

frames.action: press 'y' -- northwest, eighth and last on the slant
frames.commentary: One more and I am on the sidewalk level with the doorway.

frames.action: press 'Left' -- step west into the doorway
frames.commentary: Level with it. The leaf is swung back into the dark. In I go.

frames.action: press 'Left' -- one more west, clear of the threshold so I can shut it
frames.commentary: Under a roof. I did not know how much I minded until it was back.

frames.action: press 'c' -- shut the door behind me
frames.commentary: Now shut it. A door left open is an invitation, and I am careful.

frames.action: press 'Up' -- north up the dark aisle for the green garment I promised myself
frames.commentary: Black as a hold with the hatch on. But I said I would fetch that jacket.

frames.action: press 'Up' -- north again, stepping past the bin
frames.commentary: The bin is under my boot and slow going. Somebody emptied it and left.

frames.action: press 'Up' -- north, two more to the rack
frames.commentary: Off the bin and it charged me for the privilege both ways. Two more.

frames.action: press 'Up' -- north, level with the green garment
frames.commentary: One more and it should be off my left shoulder.

frames.action: press 'g' -- take the green garment off the rack
frames.commentary: Bright green in all this brown. Cloth between my arms and teeth counts.

frames.action: press 'Escape' -- leave it on the rack, since I cannot carry it
frames.commentary: Another golf bag, and no room for it. Promise kept, reward hollow.

frames.action: press 'bar' -- settle here in the dark and let the day pass
frames.commentary: This is my station: far side from the noise, one shut door, and glass.

frames.action: press 'w' -- choose to wait rather than set the watch to wake me
frames.commentary: Wait first. The alarm is for when I actually lie down.

frames.action: press 'k' -- sit it out until dark
frames.commentary: Eleven hours in one sitting. A skipper out in bad weather is not brave.

frames.action: press 'Y' -- stop the wait, because groaning is not a squirrel
frames.commentary: Groaning, not gargling. Lungs still trying. Stop and find out where.

frames.action: press 'bar' -- sit back down and start the wait again
frames.commentary: Northwest again, and both those doors were shut. It cannot reach me.

frames.action: press 'w' -- wait again rather than set the alarm
frames.commentary: Wait, not alarm. The alarm is for tonight.

frames.action: press 'k' -- till night again
frames.commentary: Eleven hours and forty-four minutes of it left. Again.

frames.action: press 'I' -- let the noise be and keep sitting, because I cannot flinch all day
frames.commentary: It has hit that door three times and lost. I will not flinch all day.

frames.action: press 'I' -- ignore that too, because there is nothing in the world I can do about it
frames.commentary: Withdrawals. Since nineteen and since twelve, and today they collect.

frames.action: press 'E' -- eat something before I lie down, such as it is
frames.commentary: The whole day went past me. Very thirsty is a different animal.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- eat both handfuls now, because by morning they will be rotten
frames.commentary: Thirteen calories, and rotten by dawn. Down they go, both handfuls.

frames.action: press 'I' -- ignore the craving and finish the mouthful
frames.commentary: It interrupts my supper to say I want a coffee. I am aware of it.

frames.action: press 'Return' -- eat the second handful as well, since it will be rotten by dawn
frames.commentary: The emptiness has gone. One handful left, spoiled by morning anyway.

frames.action: press 'bar' -- set the watch to wake me, the way I said I would; nothing on the screen changed
frames.commentary: Now the watch. He wore it every day and I never once set the alarm.

frames.action: press 'I' -- answer the box the only way it will accept and finish the second handful
frames.commentary: It takes only its own four answers. Ignore, then, and let me eat.

frames.action: press 'bar' -- reach for the watch now, to set it to wake me
frames.commentary: Twenty-six calories of bitter leaves. Now the watch.

frames.action: press 'dollar' -- give up on fiddling and simply lie down to sleep
frames.commentary: Never mind, it says. Fine. A shop floor is all I have wanted for hours.

frames.action: press 'Y' -- say yes and lie down
frames.commentary: Yes. Boots on, rod at my hand. Goodnight, Camille, wherever you are.

frames.action: press '8' -- set the watch for eight hours, to wake at first light
frames.commentary: Eight hours. Up when the sky goes grey, with all the light ahead of me.

frames.action: press 'I' -- ignore the craving again and stay lying down
frames.commentary: It will not even let me sleep. Stay down. Stay down, Odette.

frames.action: press 'C' -- keep trying to sleep and stop being asked about it; nothing on the screen changed
frames.commentary: Yes, I am having trouble sleeping. I will get there. Stop asking me.

frames.action: press 'I' -- ignore the craving once more and stay down
frames.commentary: It woke me to mention tobacco again. There is none. Down.

frames.action: press 'Escape' -- clear the notice and find out what woke me
frames.commentary: Survive a day and find a safe place to sleep. A golf shop floor. Well.

frames.action: press 'dollar' -- lie back down, because four hours is not a night
frames.commentary: Four hours is not a night, and four is when I said I would be up.

frames.action: press 'Y' -- yes, again
frames.commentary: Yes. Same floor, same rack, same dark. Go back down.

frames.action: press '4' -- set the watch for four hours, which lands on first light
frames.commentary: Four hours puts me at first light. Then north, to see about the willows.

frames.action: press 'I' -- push the craving aside again and keep trying to sleep
frames.commentary: Again. The small hours are when it likes to remind me. Ignore. Sleep.

frames.action: press 'C' -- keep trying to sleep and stop being asked
frames.commentary: Twenty-five minutes of turning over. No. I would rather sleep.

frames.action: press 'S' -- wake to the watch and go straight for the save and quit
frames.commentary: Beep-beep-beep. It worked. He would be unbearable about it.

frames.action: press 'Y' -- answer yes and close the day out through the door the game keeps for it
frames.commentary: One day. No water found, but I know where it is. Camille, I am still here.
